; Fall through the four-bit shifter to return A divided by 32.
; Return A divided by sixteen, dropping the low nibble.
; Return A multiplied by sixteen modulo 256.
; Return two's-complement negation of A; callers use this for signed magnitudes and angle differences.
; Shift/add unsigned mathFactor by mathMultiplier into the four-byte mathValue product. Multiplier

; Shift/add the sixteen-bit mathFactor by the low multiplier byte into a three-byte product.
; Restoring division used by distance and angle math: shift the four-byte dividend/quotient and
; remainder and subtract the three low divisor bytes. The high trial subtraction is literally
; remainderHigh minus itself; callers use small divisors, so this is not asserted to be a general
; 32-bit divisor routine.
; Continue the shared division loop and perform its final quotient shift.
; Restoring division of mathValue by mathFactor. Return quotient in mathValue and remainder in

; The successful path skips a PLA by consuming its opcode as an immediate. Borrow enters DivideTrialBorrowEntry at that $68 byte to discard the stacked trial byte.
; Divide by 100 then 10, producing three tile bytes at scratch2..4. Leading zero tiles become blanks;
; significant decimal digits have bit 7 set.
; Encode a digit as a tile, using Y to suppress only leading zeroes.
; Zero-extend A into the shared decimal converter.
; Pop the JSR return address, fetch word A from the table immediately after that JSR, and jump

; Mix the seed with its low-byte fourfold value, then add seventeen with the first sum carry

; Disable all APU channels and mark eight $15-byte software sound slots inactive using $FF cursors.
; Start three adjacent sound descriptor IDs; each call returns the following ID in A.
; Start two adjacent sound descriptor IDs.
; Preserve X and select a four-byte sound descriptor by A. Replace its assigned software slot, clear
; that channel's enable shadow when needed, and return A+1.
; Four inverted APU channel masks. DisableSoundChannel and StartSound preserve other channel-enable

; Iterate eight software slots in priority order. Initialize new tracks, advance
; duration/envelope/vibrato timers, decode events and accumulate the hardware-channel ownership mask.
; Mark this slot's channel claimed for the frame and advance to the next $15-byte slot.
; Read tempo/control/sweep bytes from its stream and initialize per-slot counters before decoding the
; first event.
; Locate the next two-byte stream event from the slot cursor; commands may consume additional
; arguments or redirect the cursor.
; Decode command classes by high nibble: loop markers, volume ramps, envelopes, counted loops, control
; commands or notes.
; $FD records a loop cursor; $FF stops the track. Other high commands skip their inline argument and
; continue.
; Store a negated ramp step and its interval for non-noise channels.
; Select an envelope and optionally its duration bound for channels using software volume control.
; Use one of two repeat counters. A zero target jumps to the saved marker; a nonzero target replaces
; the event cursor. Exhausted repeats continue after the command.
; Handle $A0 control, $A1 sweep, $A2 duty/control mode, $A3 vibrato and $A4 vibrato-disable commands;
; unrecognized values fall through as notes.
; Store the combined sound control byte and continue interpreting commands.
; Set duration and derive period from semitone and octave, or use the noise period directly. Channel
; ownership gates hardware writes.
; Clear this hardware channel's enable bit while preserving other active channel bits.
; If an earlier slot claimed this hardware channel, discard the immediate caller's return address so
; its write helper returns without touching the APU.
; Read a stream control byte and convert duty bits for pulse channels; noise uses its seven-bit
; control directly.
; Guard channel ownership before applying the current control/envelope state.
; Select triangle versus pulse/noise control registers and write the slot's current volume/control
; byte.
; Guard ownership and update envelope-driven volume when enabled; triangle is handled separately.
; Four shift/compare iterations quantize elapsed duration to sixteen phases (0..15).
; Combine phase with envelope ID * 16, then scale base volume by amplitude + 1
; and divide by sixteen. ID zero bypasses this path; IDs one/two use the two
; amplitude banks. EnvelopeAmplitudes is a biased base inside the vibrato data.
; Decrement the ramp interval and move the software control level toward its saturation endpoint.
; When enabled and its delay has elapsed, add a sixteen-phase vibrato table offset to the saved period
; low byte.
; Twelve little-endian base APU periods. PlaySoundNote accepts semitones 0..11,
; doubles the index, reads a word and shifts it right for the encoded octave.
; Four channel ownership bits (1,2,4,8), indexed by the masked channel 0..3.
; ClaimSoundChannel and GuardSoundChannel arbitrate hardware ownership with these masks.
; Four channel capability flags, indexed after channel mode AND $03.
; TickSoundEngine uses the flags for triangle/noise and volume handling.
; Three sixteen-phase signed vibrato banks. ApplySoundVibrato combines the
; encoded bank offset with frame AND $0F. Accepted streams select $00/$10/$20;
; other engine selector values do not establish further arrays.
; Two sixteen-phase nibble-amplitude banks for encoded envelope IDs one/two.
; ID one descends 15..0; ID two stays within 0..15. The CPU $B291 lookup base
; aliases the third vibrato bank: adding ID * 16 reaches ID one at $B2A1 or
; ID two at $B2B1. ID zero bypasses envelope lookup. Other IDs remain unresolved.
; Twenty-two four-byte StartSound descriptors, indexed by ID * 4: software-slot
; offset, channel mode, stream address low, stream address high. The high byte is
; ORed with $20 before use. Slot/mode encoding is preserved; names of songs and
; instruments and natural selection of every ID remain unknown. Fixed PRG [0,1,2,3].
; ID $00 -> SoundStream00
; ID $01 -> SoundStream01
; ID $02 -> SoundStream02
; ID $03 -> SoundStream03
; ID $04 -> SoundStream04
; ID $05 -> SoundStream05
